title: Sequential Thinking MCP Server
summary: Add a step-by-step reasoning tool to your agent so it can plan hard problems, revise earlier thoughts and branch, using the reference MCP server.
description: This server exposes a single tool, sequentialthinking. The agent records a numbered thought, says whether another is needed, and can mark a thought as a revision of an earlier one or start a branch.
It does not look anything up and does not touch your files. Its value is structure: a long task becomes a visible chain of steps you can read afterward.
It runs through npx over stdio and requires Node.js 24 or later.
useWhen: Plan a multi-step refactor before touching code
Work out a tricky bug where the first guess may be wrong
Compare two designs by branching the reasoning
Break a vague request into ordered tasks

mcp.name: sequential-thinking
access: Keeps the agent's thought steps in memory for the session

example.prompt: Use sequential thinking to plan how to split our 2,000 line utils.ts without breaking imports.
example.result: Thought 1 lists the export groups. Thought 2 maps each group to a new module. Thought 3 revises thought 2 after noticing a circular import. Thought 5 proposes the order of moves and a check after each.

faq.question: Does it make the model smarter?
faq.answer: It does not change the model. It gives the model a place to lay out steps and revise them, which helps on problems where a first answer is often wrong.

faq.question: Can I stop it from logging thoughts?
faq.answer: Set the environment variable DISABLE_THOUGHT_LOGGING to true. MAX_THOUGHT_HISTORY caps how many thoughts are kept per connection.
